candidates.statement: B. The USP Salt Policy is applicable to all new drug product monographs that contain a salt as the active ingredient. Titles of drug product monographs published prior to May 1, 2013, should remain unchanged, unless a modification is necessary for safety reasons. 5 USP and CDER have agreed to collaborate on any retrospective name changes that may arise.
candidates.context: A. The USP Salt Policy applies exclusively to the monograph titles of drug products and does not extend to the monograph titles of drug substances (active ingredients). The names of active ingredients, including salts, remain unaffected by this policy. C. The USP Salt Policy impacts the development of new drug products, as the title of a USP drug product monograph typically serves as the established name 6 for related drug products. A drug product that features a label or labeling that contains an established name that is not consistent with the applicable monograph title 7 may be at risk of being considered misbranded. 8

candidates.statement: I. Within the Office of Pharmaceutical Quality (OPQ) it is the responsibility of drug product Quality Assessors in the Office of Product Quality Assessment (OPQA I and II) to determine whether the USP Salt Policy applies to a new drug product. 13 The following procedures should be followed:
candidates.context: A. OPQA I and II Quality Assessors will work with the applicant at the earliest stage possible (e.g., investigational new drug (IND) phase 2) in the development of a new drug product that contains an active ingredient that is a salt. During the assessment of such a drug product, the Quality Assessors will:

candidates.statement: - The drug product established name should be based on the active moiety (not the salt) - The drug product strength should be expressed in terms of the active moiety (not the salt)

Confirmation of labeling compliance As part of the discipline-specific assessment, confirm that the drug product's labeling complies with all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements. The following confirmation checks apply:

candidates.statement: 2. Active Ingredient Requirements The use of an active moiety in the drug product established name and in the expression of strength does not impact the need to meet other statutory and regulatory requirements related to the active ingredient. For example, an applicant for an abbreviated new drug application (ANDA) must demonstrate that the generic drug product has the same active ingredient as the reference listed drug (RLD). OPQA I and II Quality Assessors confirm that other statutory and regulatory requirements related to the active ingredient have been met.
candidates.context: 1.
